items.title: MSOSH calls for safety audit after toddler's death at Victoria Bridge
items.summary: MSOSH president Datuk Ahmad Fakhrul Anuar Ismail said the audit should cover the entire visitor route, openings in the structure, the height and design of barriers, the condition of floors and walkways, lighting, warning signs, access controls and the suitability of the site for children, senior citizens and persons with disabilities. He said risk assessment records, engineering inspection reports, maintenance schedules, damage reports, previous complaints and the approval status for public access should also be examined. He said the tourism industry must also draw lessons from the incident, adding that the development of tourist destinations should not focus solely on historical value, visual appeal, promotion and visitor numbers.

items.title: Sersol sees new substantial shareholder as three directors quit
items.summary: Peh Lon Pah @ Pei Tze Chiang acquired 100 million Sersol shares, equivalent to a 12.43 per cent stake, through an off-market transaction on Sept 1, according to a Bursa Malaysia filing today. MyBursa data showed Ice Age Property Sdn Bhd as Sersol's largest shareholder with 100 million shares, equivalent to a 12.43 per cent stake. Mohamed Suffian's resignation filing, meanwhile, disclosed that he held an indirect interest in 100 million Sersol shares.

items.title: RON97, unsubsidised RON95 and diesel to drop by 5 sen from tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The retail prices of RON97 petrol, and unsubsidised RON95 petrol as well as unsubsidised diesel, will each decrease by 5 sen per litre for the period from Sept 3 to 9, 2026. The Finance Ministry (MOF) in a statement today announced that RON97 is set at RM4.25 per litre compared to RM4.30 per litre previously, while RON95 has decreased to RM3.77 from RM3.82, and unsubsidised diesel to RM4.67 from RM4.72. For Budi Diesel, recipients pay RM2.10 per litre with a government subsidy of RM2.57 per litre or 55 per cent of the unsubsidised price of RM4.67.

items.title: Second suspect arrested after Sri Petaling cable‑theft chase; remanded seven days
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Police have detained another local man to assist in investigations into a cable theft case in Sri Petaling here. Kuala Lumpur Police Chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the 32-year-old man was believed to be the driver of a Ford Ranger which was pursued on Monday from the Awan Besar Toll Plaza heading towards Klang (West) before the chase ended at Jalan Hang Tuah 4. On Monday, a police team fired several shots before detaining a 29-year-old man suspected of cable theft after the Ford Ranger driven by his accomplice attempted to flee a police inspection in Sri Petaling.

items.title: Bank manager fined RM40mil, jailed 7 years for fraud, money laundering
items.summary: KUCHING: A relationship manager with an international bank was today sentenced to seven years' jail, fined RM40 million and ordered to receive 24 strokes of the cane by the Sessions Court after pleading guilty to fraud and money laundering charges. For each of the eight money laundering charges, he was sentenced to three years' jail, with the terms to run concurrently from today, fined RM5 million or four months' jail in default, and ordered to receive one stroke of the cane. Kho failed to pay the fine.

items.title: Sunway Lagoon says all injured guests discharged, keeps roller coaster closed pending probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — The roller coaster attraction involved in the August 22, 2026 incident at Sunway Lagoon theme park in Subang Jaya, which is believed to have stopped abruptly after failing to move forward during a ride, remains closed while investigations are ongoing. “Sunway Theme Parks remains firmly committed to maintaining the highest standards of safety and to ensuring the well-being of everyone who visits our parks,” it said. Sunway Theme Parks confirms that all guests who were admitted to the hospital for further observation following the incident have now been discharged.

items.title: Ringgit weakens against US dollar, mixed against other major currencies
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit continued to trade lower against the US dollar on Wednesday but strengthened against the British pound and the euro amid rising global bond yields and concerns over elevated government debt levels. At 6pm, the ringgit was quoted at 4.0435/0475 against the US dollar compared with Tuesday's close of 4.0370/0410. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said rising bond yields currently remained the main focus, particularly in developed markets.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Wednesday, Sept 2, 2026
items.summary: MISSED what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. [[nid:1524464]] [[nid:1524463]] [[nid:1524462]] [[nid:1524461]] [[nid:1524460]] © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: SMART prepared for Nepal deployment, with logistics and personnel on standby, says commander
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — The Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) has its personnel and logistics on standby for possible deployment to Nepal. “The SMART team is ready physically and mentally, and prepared for any deployment for this mission. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim previously said SMART would assist in search and rescue (SAR) operations in Nepal following the flood disaster, including locating and bringing home affected Malaysians.

items.title: Perhilitan relocates elephant ‘Sulong Chalil’ to Terengganu Taman Negara after Gerik recapture
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 2 — A wild male elephant known as “Sulong Chalil” has been relocated today to Terengganu Taman Negara through the Tasik Kenyir entrance, a natural forest habitat suitable for wild elephants. The department said that since Aug 17, the Perhilitan team has been closely monitoring Sulong’s movements and physical condition, including the injury recorded on his right leg. “Throughout the operation, Sulong always received monitoring and veterinary treatment.

items.title: Putrajaya MRT Line service disrupted following signalling issue
items.summary: Rapid KL, in a statement, said alternative train services and free shuttle buses had been activated to help commuters continue their journeys while waiting for a solution to the disruption. "The alternative train services involve trains from Kentonmen station turning back at Raja Uda, while trains from Raja Uda will turn back at Chan Sow Lin. "Free shuttle buses are operating between Kwasa Damansara and Kepong Baru, stopping at Kampung Selamat, Sungai Buloh, Damansara Damai, Sri Damansara Barat, Sri Damansara Sentral, Sri Damansara Timur and Metro Prima," it said in a social media post.

items.title: Ramssol inks RM31mil AI, IT deal with Linear Channel
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Ramssol Group Bhd has teamed up with Linear Channel Sdn Bhd to provide information technology devices, artificial intelligence (AI) solutions and device monitoring software. The RM30.94 million partnership, undertaken through Ramssol's unit Rams Aitech Sdn Bhd, will support Linear Channel's GreenElite Pro device-as-a-service programme. Under the programme, Linear Channel contracts directly with small and medium enterprise customers to rent information technology equipment bundled with AI software and device fleet monitoring services.

items.title: Haze leaves Kuching riverside traders counting losses
items.summary: Trader Nony Rusley, who has operated her stall there since 2022, said her daily takings could previously reach RM1,000 but had fallen as the haze worsened. "Usually, people would start arriving in large numbers from 3pm. "Usually, many people would come with their families.

items.title: Teen feared drowned after telling friend he couldn't swim
items.summary: He said the teen, who was pursuing his studies at a college, had previously told him that he could not swim. "He had told me that he could not swim, but his father had previously said that he could swim," he said when contacted today. Melaka Fire and Rescue Department public relations officer Assistant Fire Superintendent II Mohd Hafidzatullah Rashid said a team led by Operations Commander Senior Fire Officer I Mohd Soffian Hassan rushed to the scene.

items.title: Police obtain four‑day remand for boat operator in fatal Mersing collision that left two dead
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 2 — A boat operator involved in the incident where two passenger boats collided in Kuala Sungai Mersing, killing two people last Sunday, has been remanded for four days starting today. Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the 33-year-old local man was arrested by a Criminal Investigation Division team of the Mersing district police headquarters (IPD) at about 12 noon yesterday to assist in the investigation. He said the suspect was then taken to the Kota Tinggi Magistrate’s Court for a remand application under Section 117 of the Criminal Procedure Code.

items.title: PPC orders probe into Teluk Bahang ferry collision
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH: The Penang Port Commission (PPC) has ordered a special investigation into the cause of the Teluk Bahang ferry collision that injured 21 people last night. PPC chairman Datuk Yeoh Soon Hin said the team, comprising the commission and ferry operator Penang Port Sdn Bhd, would conduct an objective, transparent and professional investigation. The incident occurred at 8.40pm yesterday when the Teluk Bahang ferry, travelling from Pangkalan Raja Tun Uda in George Town to Pangkalan Sultan Abdul Halim in Butterworth, collided with cargo vessel MV Mekar Jaya within Penang Port limits.

items.title: Macau chief executive begins working visit to Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Macau Special Administrative Region Chief Executive Sam Hou Fai will undertake a four-day working visit to Malaysia from today to Sept 5. The Foreign Ministry, in a statement today, said that during the visit, Sam is scheduled to pay a courtesy call on Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. This will be Sam's first visit to Malaysia since assuming office as Macau's fourth chief executive in 2024.

items.title: Former Tabung Haji COO to be charged in Shah Alam Sessions Court tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — A former Lembaga Tabung Haji chief operating officer is expected to be charged at the Shah Alam Sessions Court tomorrow. The Star reported that a court e‑filing entry lists Datuk Adi Azuan Abdul Ghani as scheduled to appear before Sessions Court judge Awang Kerisnada Awang Mahmud at 9am on September 3. The arrests include a former Tabung Haji investment director, the director of Putrajaya Perdana, the former director of Putra Perdana Construction, the former Tabung Haji chairman, the chief executive officer of Alam Maritim and a former federal minister.

items.title: PHB expands AHB fund with 400mil new units
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pelaburan Hartanah Bhd (PHB) has announced the issuance of 400 million new units of Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera (AHB) for subscription by Bumiputera investors, raising the fund's total units to 5.4 billion. PHB said the additional units reaffirmed its commitment to expanding opportunities for Bumiputera to gain beneficial ownership of quality commercial properties through investments in strategically located commercial real estate assets nationwide. Investors can subscribe to AHB units at authorised distributor branches nationwide, including Maybank, AmBank, AmBank Islamic, Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd and Bank Kerjasama Rakyat Malaysia Bhd.

items.title: Pandemic delays behind payment backlog, says Rural Development Ministry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Rural and Regional Development Ministry (KKDW) has denied claims by the Finance Ministry (MoF) that it overspent its parliamentary allocation, saying payment backlogs stemmed from delayed commitments made during the Covid-19 pandemic, rather than financial mismanagement. KKDW press secretary Fadzmel Fadzil said portraying the ministry as having spent beyond its allocation gave an inaccurate picture of government financial procedures. "Government financial procedure does not allow any ministry to simply spend beyond its approved allocation.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM SEPT 02, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia's 30-stock index closed higher on Thursday lifted by gains in oil-related and plantation stocks. The key index rose more than eight points to 1,708. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Sultan Nazrin graces Maha 2026
items.summary: SERDANG: The Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah today graced the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism (Maha) Exhibition 2026 at the Malaysia Agro Exposition Park Serdang (MAEPS). Raja Permaisuri of Perak Tuanku Zara Salim and Raja Kecil Besar Raja Azlan Muzzaffar Shah accompanied him on the visit. Sultan Nazrin, Tuanku Zara and Raja Azlan visited several booths at the Perak Pavilion.

items.title: Minister: National Scam Response Centre returned RM5.16m to victims, from funds seized between January and July 2026
items.summary: “For us, the return of money to victims is among the enforcement outcomes that can be directly felt by the people,” he said at a press conference after officiating the 6th International Cyber Resilience Conference (CRC) here today. He said the figures also indicated that cyber threats were becoming increasingly serious, with the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) reporting that scam operations in Southeast Asia alone generated tens of billions of dollars annually. Touching on figures for online sexual abuse, he said cases involving child sexual abuse material (CSAM) increased from 68 in 2024 to 152 last year, while another 100 cases were recorded up to the middle of this year.

items.title: Cargo vessel hits Sungai Johor Bridge in Kota Tinggi
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: A cargo vessel is believed to have struck the Sungai Johor Bridge along the Senai-Desaru Expressway (SDE) here today. The New Straits Times learnt that the bridge structure remained intact, with no major defects or damage reported. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Felda pledges full cooperation as MACC opens six probes into agency, FIC
items.summary: In a statement today, Felda said it fully respected the ongoing investigation process to ensure that it was carried out transparently, fairly and comprehensively. Felda also called on all parties to respect the investigation process. MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said today that the commission had opened six new investigation papers into allegations of misappropriation, abuse of power and corruption involving Felda and its subsidiary, Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC).

items.title: Anwar warns US-Iran hostilities risk wider regional conflict, urges return to diplomacy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today urged the United States (US) and Iran to immediately halt further escalation and return to diplomacy amid renewed hostilities between the two countries. No military objective justifies exposing civilians to an expanding conflict,” he said. “I urge the United States and Iran to halt further escalation and return immediately to diplomacy and the understandings reached in June,” he said.

items.title: Deadly rough seas: Three beach incidents in Kota Tinggi in four days
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: Three people have drowned and three teenagers remain missing following three separate incidents at beaches in the district in just four days. Four 16-year-old boys were swept away while swimming at Pantai Tanjung Lompat, Bandar Desaru here, this morning. The three others still missing are Muhammad Thaqif Rayyan Rumainoor, Mohamad Haiman Fitri Supian and Muhammad Adib Hafiy Kamal.

items.title: Petronas to sustain production at 2mil barrels of oil equivalent per day through 2028
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) aims to sustain Malaysia's oil and gas production at two million barrels of oil equivalent per day (mmboe/d) through 2028, said its president and group chief executive officer Tan Sri Tengku Muhammad Taufik Tengku Aziz today. He said the target would be anchored in continued investment across exploration, deep-water development, and enhanced recovery from Petronas' producing fields. Across its portfolio, Tengku Muhammad Taufik said the national oil company is applying the same approach through partnerships, technical collaborations and alternative commercial structures tailored to the circumstances of individual opportunities.

items.title: Anwar warns US-Iran strikes risk wider Middle East conflict
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today urged the United States and Iran to immediately halt further escalation and return to diplomacy amid renewed hostilities between the two countries. No military objective justifies exposing civilians to an expanding conflict," he said in a Facebook post. "I urge the United States and Iran to halt further escalation and return immediately to diplomacy and the understandings reached in June," he said.

items.title: Claim on Malaysia recruiting 200,000 Bangladeshi workers not Bangladesh’s official position, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — A statement by a Bangladeshi junior minister claiming that Malaysia planned to recruit 200,000 workers from the country does not represent the official position of the Bangladeshi government, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. He said Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R Ramanan had confirmed that a junior member had made the statement on behalf of the Bangladesh government and that it did not represent the country’s official position. Meanwhile, Fahmi said the Cabinet had been informed that 1,476 Myanmar nationals held at immigration detention depots would be repatriated to their home country at the end of this month.

items.title: Melaka polls a test of BN-PN cooperation, says analyst
items.summary: He said BN had reason to be confident in Melaka given the state's strong Umno grassroots organisation, with the coalition's landslide win in the last state election cementing its position as the dominant force there. "PN should not enter negotiations demanding an equal seat split without taking into account the reality of local strength on the ground. He said among the formulas that could be considered was a split of 20 seats for BN and eight for PN, or 21 seats for BN and seven for PN, based on winnability.

items.title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain to hit KL and 12 states until 7pm, says MetMalaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Kuala Lumpur and 12 states until 7pm tonight. MetMalaysia in a statement today announced that the bad weather is expected to occur throughout Perlis, Kedah, Terengganu as well as three areas in Penang including Seberang Perai Utara, Seberang Perai Tengah dan Seberang Perai Selatan. Similar warnings have also been issued for Selangor (Hulu Selangor, Gombak and Hulu Langat), Negeri Sembilan (Tampin, Rembau, Jelebu, Seremban, Jempol and Kuala Pilah), and Johor (Segamat).

items.title: Wildfire haze forces 1.4 million Indonesian students into remote learning
items.summary: JAKARTA: Around 1.4 million students in six Indonesian provinces have shifted to online learning due to poor air quality triggered by forest and land fires, an official said on Wednesday. As of Sept 2, around 1.43 million students from 12,874 schools in six of the provinces hit hardest by forest and land fires have been studying remotely, Gogot Suharwoto, an education ministry official, told the media. Of the 1.43 million students, 1.1 million are in West Kalimantan, Gogot said, the province that has recorded the most extensive wildfires so far this year.

items.title: UKM denies convicted ex-student is university staff
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM) has denied that Nur Fitri Azmeer Nordin, who was previously convicted in Britain of possessing child sexual abuse material, is a staff member at the university. In a statement today, UKM said Nur Fitri had completed his Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) at the university in 2021. "UKM denies that Nur Fitri Azmeer is a UKM staff member.

items.title: Fahmi: Sarawak’s Malaysia Day celebration to be held indoors at BCCK; outdoor events off due to haze
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — Malaysia Day 2026 celebrations on September 16 will be held as scheduled at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK), Sarawak, but outdoor events cannot be held due to the worrying haze situation in Kuching and Serian. Communications Minister and chairman of the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day Celebrations (HKHM) Main Committee Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the decision was made after taking into account the haze situation in both areas. “The Cabinet also took note that the rather worrying haze situation in Kuching and Serian means that outdoor events cannot proceed.

items.title: Mudajaya, China Communications Construction dispute widens with RM17.6mil claim
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Mudajaya Group Bhd's unit, Mudajaya Corp Bhd, has served a second payment claim against China Communications Construction (ECRL) Sdn Bhd (CCC) totalling RM17.56 million amid an ongoing dispute linked to the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) project. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said the claim relates to unpaid certified amounts under CCC's interim payment certificates, under-certified and uncertified work done, uncertified variations and wrongful contra charges. Mudajaya filed an adjudication in December 2025 under the Construction Industry Payment and Adjudication Act 2012 (CIPAA), seeking RM10.95 million from CCC over under-certified claims for Package 3 of the ECRL.

items.title: Treat haze as annual health threat, not seasonal nuisance, pharmacists urge public
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians should treat transboundary haze as a recurring public health threat and prepare for it before air quality deteriorates, the Malaysian Pharmacists Society (MPS) said. Its president, Professor Amrahi Buang, said families should not regard haze merely as a temporary inconvenience, particularly when exposure to fine particulate matter continues over several days. He said children, older adults, pregnant women and people with chronic respiratory or cardiovascular conditions should reduce time spent outdoors and avoid strenuous activity when the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings worsen.

items.title: MACC ready to probe N. Sembilan Pakatan allocation if misuse proven, says commissioner
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is ready to investigate if there is evidence of misuse involving the RM180,000 allocation granted to each Pakatan Harapan (PH) state assemblyman prior to the dissolution of the Negeri Sembilan State Assembly on June 5. MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said reports accompanied by evidence showing fund misuse or legal offences would serve as a basis for the commission to initiate an investigation. Meanwhile, in a separate case, Abd Halim said the MACC had yet to receive a letter regarding a corruption case involving former human resources minister Datuk Seri M. Saravanan.

items.title: Felda pledges cooperation in MACC probe into seven cases
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Felda has pledged cooperation with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) in the graft buster's probe involving the agency and its subsidiaries. Halim said six of the cases involved new investigations, while the case involving Grand Borneo Hotel Sdn Bhd was a continuation of a previous probe. The seven cases involve Dataran Aras Sdn Bhd, Grand Borneo Hotel Sdn Bhd, Merdeka Palace Hotel and Suites, Park City Grand Plaza Kensington, Felda Wellness Corporation Sdn Bhd, Felda House and Grand Felda House, as well as the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project.

items.title: Serian and Kuching record hazardous API levels in Sarawak at 4pm; more areas very unhealthy
items.summary: According to the Malaysian API Management System (APIMS), Kuching recorded a hazardous API reading of 309. Meanwhile, five areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy API readings: Samarahan (287), Sarikei (256), Sibu (248), Sri Aman (247) and Mukah (205). Forty-five stations recorded API readings at the moderate level, while none recorded readings in the good category.

items.title: 5.5-magnitude quake hits northeast of New Zealand's Milford Sound
items.summary: WELLINGTON: A 5.5-magnitude earthquake struck 40 kilometres northeast of Milford Sound on New Zealand's South Island on Wednesday, the country's earthquake monitoring agency reported. The quake, at a depth of 5km, struck at 6.13pm local time and was classified as moderate, according to GeoNet, which said nearly 7,000 people had reported feeling it. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Tiong: Don't make assumptions over Tun M's National Day appearance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing has urged the public not to make assumptions over Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad's presence at the National Day celebration on Aug 31, saying the controversy should be viewed based on facts and established protocol. Tiong said he understood that Mahathir had obtained Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's approval to travel to Thailand from Aug 28 to 31. However, he said he was unaware that Mahathir's travel plans had subsequently changed.

items.title: EU's Kallas says Leipzig attack had hallmarks of state-sponsored terrorism
items.summary: WICKLOW: The attempted attack in Leipzig had all the hallmarks of state-sponsored terrorism, the European Union's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said on Wednesday, adding that Europe needs to coordinate on what more can be done given the escalation of Russia's attacks on Ukraine. The German government said on Tuesday that it had concluded that Russia was responsible for the attempted drone attack at Leipzig/Halle airport last month. Lithuania's Foreign Minister Kestutis Budrys said Europeans need to consider their options and respond.

items.title: Woman found in bag in Sungai Perak was bound before being dumped – Police
items.summary: Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the victim, believed to be in her 30s, was suspected to have drowned, but her identity remained unknown. Alwi said police would work with relevant agencies, including the Immigration Department and Interpol, to obtain information to establish the victim's identity. In a separate development, Alwi said police would investigate allegations of gambling activities at several premises in Taiping that had gone viral on social media.

items.title: MACC: Six Felda and FIC cases under investigation, arrests imminent
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has opened six new investigation papers into alleged misappropriation, abuse of power and corruption involving the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) and its subsidiary, Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC), with several arrests expected beginning next week. MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the investigations followed information received on Aug 24 regarding the implementation of projects and investments by Felda and FIC management between 2010 and 2020. The six matters are the purchase of Tataran Aras Sdn Bhd in Limbang, Sarawak; the acquisition of Grand Borneo Hotel Sdn Bhd in Sabah; the purchase of Grand Plaza Serviced Apartments in London; the establishment of Felda Wellness Corporation Sdn Bhd; the acquisition of Felda House and Grand Felda House; and alleged misappropriation in the development of the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project.

items.title: Perak police launch investigations over toddler’s fatal fall at Victoria Bridge
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 2 — Police have opened two investigation papers into the death of a three-year-old boy who is believed to have fallen about five metres from Victoria Bridge in Enggor, near Kuala Kangsar, yesterday. Perak Police Chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the investigation papers were opened under Section 31(1) of the Child Act 2001, with several individuals summoned to assist the investigation. Meanwhile, State Housing and Local Government Committee chairperson Sandrea Ng Shy Ching said the Kuala Kangsar Municipal Council (MPKK) had immediately closed visitor access to the steel structure section of the bridge as a safety measure.

items.title: MACC investigator: Muhyiddin abused powers as PM to help Jana Wibawa contractors
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin abused his powers as a prime minister when he acted to help Bumiputera contractors to eventually get government projects under the Jana Wibawa programme, an anti-corruption investigator told the High Court. When asked by Wan Shaharuddin to explain why he said Muhyiddin had abused his powers as prime minister, Mazery said this was due to Muhyiddin’s actions in relation to companies who were applying for Jana Wibawa projects. Muhyiddin was prime minister from March 1, 2020 until Aug 20, 2021.

items.title: Don’t sacrifice independent oversight for speed in Sabah’s water crisis fixes, says former Water Dept director
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 2 — Sabah’s recurring water supply problems require urgent and practical solutions, but the push for faster action should not come at the expense of independent engineering judgement, said Datuk Amarjit Singh. The former Sabah Water Department director said a clear distinction must be maintained between an engineering consultancy practice and a commercial service provider, particularly when companies supplying water infrastructure, equipment, or specialised technologies are also proposing solutions. Amarjit said companies recommending technologies in which they have a commercial interest could face an inherent potential conflict, making independent assessment important.

items.title: Batik Air agrees to resume Miri-KL flights after deputy minister’s request
items.summary: MIRI, Sept 2 — Batik Air has agreed to resume its Miri-Kuala Lumpur services following a formal request by Deputy Minister of Tourism, Arts and Culture Chiew Choon Man. The Miri MP said the commencement date, flight frequency and schedule would be announced by the airline in due course. Chiew said he had received increasing feedback from Miri residents over the difficulty of securing flights between Miri and Kuala Lumpur, particularly during weekends, public holidays and peak travel periods.

items.title: Retiree loses RM1.417m after transferring savings across multiple accounts in phone‑call scam
items.summary: Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the victim, a 66-year-old man, received a call from an unknown individual on May 19 who claimed that the victim was involved in money laundering activities. He said the victim was then instructed to open an Agrobank account and transfer his savings to the account for the purpose of checking by the authorities. “After opening the account, a man came to meet the victim in his residential area and the victim handed over his bank card and PIN number to the man,” he said in a statement.

items.title: US embassy shifts Sabah travel status to ‘relaxed’ after security improvements
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 2 — The United States is encouraging its citizens and international travellers to visit Sabah, citing significant improvements in security and a corresponding relaxation of travel advisories, said US Embassy Kuala Lumpur Chargé d'Affaires David Gamble. Many countries are following America’s lead and reviewing their travel advisories as well,” Gamble said during the launch of the Freedom 250 Sabah programme at the Tanjung Aru State Library today. We want to encourage more tourists to visit Sabah because Sabah is a wonderful place to visit.”

items.title: Johor dengue cases jump 131pc to 9,954 as infections rise across districts
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 2 — Johor recorded 9,954 dengue cases as of Epid Week (ME) 34 this year, an increase of 131.3 per cent compared to 4,304 cases for the same period last year. State Health and Environment Committee Chairman Ling Tian Soon said of the total, 4,520 cases or 45.4 per cent were reported from outbreak localities while 5,434 cases or 54.6 per cent were from non-outbreak localities. “Of the total dengue cases reported throughout ME34, 308 cases or 46.4 per cent were reported from outbreak localities and 356 cases or 53.6 per cent from non-outbreak localities,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: One teen found dead as search continues for three others missing in Tanjung Balau
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 2 — The body of one of four teenagers feared drowned at Tanjung Lompat Beach in Tanjung Balau was recovered this afternoon. The victim, identified as Alif Taqiudin Kamal Hasrul Mohamad, was found by the search and rescue (SAR) team and members of the public at 1.25pm, approximately 800 metres from the location where he was last seen. Kota Tinggi police chief Deputy Superintendent Mohd Syamsuri Mohamad confirmed that the body was identified by family members and has since been transported to Kota Tinggi Hospital.

items.title: MMEA detains tugboat and dredger over suspected ship‑to‑ship transfer; RM260m oil cargo seized off Tanjung Buai
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 2 — The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) detained two vessels suspected of carrying out unauthorised ship-to-ship activities in national waters early yesterday morning, with the value of the seized goods estimated at RM260 million. Tanjung Sedili Zone Maritime acting director Maritime Commander Mohd Najib Sam said the action was carried out at 3.20am after receiving public information regarding two suspicious vessels seen huddled together at a position about 1.4 nautical miles northwest of Tanjung Buai. Mohd Najib said the tugboat was operated by a crew of five including the skipper, consisting of local and Indonesian citizens aged between 26 and 58 years, while the dredger was operated by a crew of 13 including the skipper, all local citizens aged between 22 and 51 years.

items.title: VIPs and officials in crosshairs as MACC readies charges for multiple suspects in TH probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is moving to charge several individuals over the next two days following a massive probe into the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji (TH). MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said that the upcoming charges centre on the alleged abuse of power and misappropriation of RM334.2 million linked to investments in TH Marine, TH Alam, and TH Alam Management, FMT reported. “Another charge involves alleged corruption related to TH’s 30 per cent stake in construction company Putrajaya Perdana Bhd.

items.title: Man remanded after viral video of provocative act at National Day celebration in Putrajaya
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — A man in his 30s, believed to be involved in a provocative incident during the 69th National Day celebrations last Monday, has been remanded for one day starting today. Putrajaya police chief Assistant Commissioner Aidi Sham Mohamed confirmed the arrest when contacted. “The suspect has been remanded for one day starting today,” he said.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh’s official website confirms divorce after 18-year marriage
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh and her husband Ramachandran Muniandy have divorced after 18 years of marriage. Yeoh was later appointed Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) in December 2025. Within DAP, Yeoh currently serves as deputy secretary-general, vice-chair of DAP and a committee member of DAP Wanita.

items.title: ‘Not a coincidence’: Contractors’ RM25.3m to Bersatu came after Muhyiddin’s aid to get projects, was not ‘political donation’, court told
items.summary: Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigating officer Mazery Mohd Zaini said the RM25.3 million was instead a reward given after Bersatu president and former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin helped these companies get government projects. Mazery said this while testifying as the 29th prosecution witness in Muhyiddin’s abuse‑of‑power and money‑laundering trial. Mazery said the RM25.3 million was not a genuine donation.

items.title: Sabah activates state and district disaster command centres as API readings rise to unhealthy levels
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 2 — Sabah has activated its State Disaster Operations Command Centre (PKOB), as well as district-level PKOBs in Kota Kinabalu, Keningau and Papar, as the Air Pollutant Index (API) rose yesterday. State Secretary Datuk Zainudin Aman, who is also State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) chairman, said that API readings reached worrying unhealthy levels yesterday in Kota Kinabalu (177), Tawau (153), Keningau (165), Kimanis, Papar (166) and Kota Kinabalu Polytechnic (153). Zainudin said a haze emergency or disaster would be declared when API readings reached 500 and above.

items.title: PPC orders formation of special task force to probe Penang ferry-cargo vessel collision
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 2 — Authorities have ordered the formation of a special task force to investigate last night’s collision between the Teluk Bahang Ferry and cargo vessel MV Mekar Jaya in Penang Port waters. Penang Port Commission (PPC) Chairman Datuk Yeoh Soon Hin said the task force would investigate the cause of the incident and determine the circumstances surrounding the collision. Yeoh said relevant parties have also been instructed to gather information and assist with compensation matters.
